entry.title: Ways to try: Re-checked 10 Nov in a headless browser without a GPU: 4 of 4 of the demos we first checked on 6 Oct ran (20 Oct: 4 of 4); the fifth, neural-canvas, is re-checked separately. Fly Worker, re-checked 10 Nov after a change to its model code: ran by our check's rule, and two screenshots of its game panel taken about 7 seconds apart show its street game view, frame counter and brain-activity dots changing. It downloaded about 8.6 MB of brain data, identified by their web address, a method we fixed before this check. In our browser checks from 3 Oct to 10 Nov 2026, 8 of 13 demos ran on a machine without a GPU at their latest check.

Ways to try, Overview and For AI agents: Correction, 10 Nov 2026: our earlier overall line said 9 of 13 demos ran. That was the 20 Oct count, and we did not update it after the re-checks of 24 to 31 Oct, in which neural-canvas, flyleno and help-the-fly-escape stopped responding and fly-brain-lulzx was stopped by its memory use. At each demo's latest check, 8 of 13 ran.

Controls ledger: two studies joined. indian-aman's whole-CNS specificity study (MaleCNS v1.0): the steering readout stays at 4.11 Hz (real 3.98 Hz) when wiring is shuffled within cell type and side, and falls to -0.01 Hz under a whole-CNS shuffle, so the ledger reads mixed; no no-brain baseline was run. Authors' numbers from a GPU run, not re-run by us. Kishandev12's signal study: real wiring spread activity further than degree-preserving rewiring (about 137 vs 107 active downstream neurons, 10 of 10 pairs). This measures how far activity spreads, not a task, so we do not score it as the wiring helping; no no-brain baseline was run. Authors' numbers, not re-run by us. 107 studies, 97 with a wiring null; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 36 of 97.

Catalogue: 213 entries (2 new). Re-read 10 Nov after code changes: NeuroCraft Fly moves from U to C: its source is now public, and its readouts select scripted body programs. Re-read 10 Nov after code changes: Fly Worker keeps A. Fly Worker's own numbers after a steering-bias fix (author's numbers, not re-run by us): the fly brain covers 50% of the game map, smoothed noise 63% and uniform noise 49%; a fly brain shown a different board scores 66%. The author withdraws the earlier -3 point paired result. There is still no comparison with scrambled wiring. Re-read 10 Nov after changes: flyshi-research keeps B. Re-checked 10 Nov: 22 of the 24 projects we graded on 20-21 Oct keep their grade (1 after a full re-read of changed files); 2 could not be re-checked because the source is no longer public. Two batch entries could not be re-checked: the source repositories of ascend and connectomics-fly-whole-brain-nulls returned 404 (checked 10 Nov 2026); each grade is for the code we read on its grade date (20 and 21 Oct 2026). flylab-demo: its source repository could not be reached on 9 and 10 Nov 2026 (not found); its grade (C) is for the code we read on 30 Oct 2026.

Is it real?: new verdict row. 'What Is It Like to Be a Fly?' (Andrew Sheerin, free browser gamebook, shared from 6 Nov 2026) replays spike recordings from published fly-brain models (Shiu et al. 2024 on FlyWire data); the movements and two of its six scenes are written by the author, as its own note says. The model does not run in the page, and no code repository is linked (page read 10 Nov 2026).

New report: Thirty-first check (10 Nov 2026), five browser demos re-checked with the latest check of all 13, the count correction, two new control studies, re-reads, the re-check of 24 projects, the gamebook verdict and the lead scan.

Is it real? and Does fly wiring help?: We re-ran the authors' nerve-cord walking model on an ordinary 2-processor server without a GPU (9 Nov 2026): with the real front-leg wiring, 3 motor neurons showed a regular rhythm; with the wiring shuffled by the authors' own shuffle, 4 of 5 tries still showed a rhythm (0, 12, 40, 3 and 1 motor neurons in the 5 tries). One run each, faster solver settings than the paper, no noise. The authors' shuffle keeps each neuron's excitatory or inhibitory sign and shuffles connections within each cell group; it differs from the shuffle used for their circuit-pattern count. The shuffled circuits were far more active than the real one (1,645 to 1,995 active cells against 97; top firing rates about 230 against 16 per second), so this is not a like-for-like comparison; a test with activity matched has not been run. By the rule we fixed before the run (if at least half of the shuffles still show a rhythm, our row reads no difference), our own row reads no difference. The catalogue entry for the paper stays not tested.

Controls ledger: one new row made by us (pugliese-2026-shuffle-check, no difference by the rule fixed before the run, not activity-matched); 105 studies, 95 with a wiring null, fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 36 of 95.

"Uploaded" fly-brain videos: A new Urdu and Hindi video, 'Scientists Uploaded a Fly's Brain Into a Computer Are Humans Next?' (Takhti, 3 Nov 2026; about 202,000 views on 9 Nov), uses the word uploaded in its title, while its own description says this does not mean a fly's mind was copied and calls Eon Systems' demos company claims with limits. That matches the primary sources: a wiring map traced from one preserved fly brain, run as a simplified model. We read the title and description, not the video (checked 9 Nov 2026).

9 Nov: we scanned news, videos and new code from 3 to 9 Nov; one widely seen new video, an Urdu and Hindi explainer whose title says a fly's brain was uploaded, got a dated check (its own description says no mind was copied). Two new write-ups about fly-brain games and puzzles and several small new code projects that say they test whether the fly's wiring matters are queued for a first look. Tracking: Links as on 2 Nov; 57 of 57 videos available; 9 tracked repositories with new commits since 2 Nov were recorded and not yet re-read.

New report: Thirtieth check (9 Nov 2026), the walking-circuit model re-run with the real wiring and 5 shuffles, with active neurons shown beside the rhythm counts, specs (One simulation took 1.2 minutes and its process peaked at 1.4 GB of memory; the software and wiring data used about 1,130 MB of disk.), limits and next steps.

Build your own: Re-test, 2 November 2026: 6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact. The beginner path re-run from an empty folder on 2 Nov 2026 (Linux x86_64, Python 3.11.2, 2 CPUs, no GPU) with the pinned packages, and again with the short requirements.txt command (6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz). No page fixes were needed. On 2 Nov 2026 the short requirements.txt command installed 7 newer helper packages than our exact lock (Cython 3.3.0 → 3.3.1, iniconfig 2.3.0 → 2.3.1, MarkupSafe 3.0.3 → 3.0.4, pluggy 1.6.0 → 1.7.0, python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0 → 4.0.0, pytz 2026.4 → 2026.6, tzdata 2026.4 → 2026.6) and gave 82.0 Hz; the six main packages are pinned and did not change. It also did not install the package six, which is in our lock (python-dateutil 4.0.0 appears not to need it; we did not check its metadata). Use requirements.lock to get exactly our environment.

What do I need to run it? (updated 2 Nov 2026): Device: Python 3.11; on 2 Nov 2026 we used 2 CPUs and no GPU (no NVIDIA device or driver present; Brian2 used its RuntimeDevice with the numpy code target, which the demo picks because the host has no C++ compiler). The simulation process itself peaked at 0.59 GB of memory for one 1-second trial, and the tests at 0.61 GB. These figures are the largest single process (measured with getrusage), not the whole test container, which peaked at about 1.7 GB including file cache and the parent process. The folder took about 660 MB of disk: a 464 MB Python environment and a 196 MB model folder with its data.

Pins: unchanged; checked against PyPI on 2 Nov 2026 (latest: Brian2 2.11.0, numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.1.0, mujoco 3.17.0; our pins stay at 2.9.0, 2.3.5, 2.3.3 and 3.9.0), and the Brian2, numpy and pandas pins installed cleanly in the re-test of 2 Nov (mujoco, the body pin, was not re-installed); next re-test due 16 Nov 2026. On 2 Nov the first sugar trial took 96 to 112 s from start to finish and the tests 77 to 87 s, longer than on 19 Oct (68 s and 58 s); we do not know why.

2 Nov: we scanned news, videos and new code from 1 to 2 Nov; nothing met the bar for a new claim check. Tracking: 2 Nov 2026: we looked up the latest commit of 142 tracked repositories again: 4 have new commits since 31 Oct, recorded and not judged yet; flydoom is still gone or private. The repositories of 13 of the 25 verdict rows were re-checked, none with new code since 31 Oct. Links as on 31 Oct (fruitfly.live still fails its security certificate; the ascend demo and the FlyGym browser viewer still answer 404). 57 of 57 videos available.

New report: Twenty-ninth check (2 Nov 2026), the beginner guide re-tested from an empty folder with the pinned lock and with the short command, what the memory numbers measure, why we say no GPU, pins, run times, and limits.

211 catalogue entries (31 Oct 2026): 2 new: fly-hearing-lab A (worse) and drosocode A (worse, one run each). Re-read: fly-naf B kept, now with a wiring control (Fly-NAF (re-read 31 Oct): the author now tests the wiring. On one replayed game night the real wiring answered 7 of 8 threats on the threat's side first; three shuffled brains answered 0, 3 and 3. The game constants were tuned on the real wiring, so the shuffled brains ran with settings made for another network. Grade B kept.); flybrain-prove-ai A kept; fly-connectome-reservoir B kept. neural-canvas: The copy of this demo at fruitfly.live answered on 30 and 31 Oct with a security certificate made for its hosting service's own addresses, not for fruitfly.live, so browsers refuse to open it; this looks like a setup problem at that address, which we did not check further. The Hugging Face version is the one we link.

Controls ledger (31 Oct 2026): 3 new rows (fly-naf helps, rated unfair because its constants were tuned on the real wiring; fly-hearing-lab and drosocode worse), now 104 studies, 94 with a wiring null: helps 36, no difference 26, worse 11, mixed 17, not yet scored 4; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 36 of 94. Pugliese stays not scored. Scoring unchanged.

31 Oct: we scanned news, videos and new code from 30 to 31 Oct; nothing met the bar for a new claim check, our news searches found no new coverage of the walking-circuit paper beyond the journal article itself, and two new code projects with their own scrambled-wiring tests were added. Pugliese et al. 2026 (Nature): We checked whether the authors' walking model can be re-run with shuffled wiring on an ordinary 2-processor server without a GPU (31 Oct 2026): its software would need an estimated 620 MB once installed, plus 86 MB of wiring data, more than our 600 MB test space. The test was not run. The authors' shuffle keeps each neuron's excitatory or inhibitory sign and shuffles connections within each cell group; it differs from the shuffle used for their circuit-pattern count. Whether the real wiring is needed for the simulated walking rhythm stays not tested; the earlier circuit count is a pattern in the wiring, not a test of walking.

fly67: runs again on 31 Oct. It downloaded about 33 MB of brain data, identified by their web address, a method we fixed before this check. Checked in headless Chromium 154.0.8037.57 on a Linux server without a GPU, 31 Oct 2026. Shows whether the page loads, downloads its brain data and keeps computing; it is not a play test. Safari, Firefox, phones and GPU machines were not tested.
